content:
I have recently removed various imports in mathlib and its dependencies, which has lead to about a 5% speedup in mathlib due to faster import times. Now, I've made a testing PR (#40753) that avoids importing suggestion features into Mathlib, such as try?, grind +suggestions and apply?. This gives another 0.77% speedup. The reason is that removing these imports also avoids importing lots of grind internals that are completely redundant for mathlib (note that these are not needed for calling grind, because grind is a builtin tactic).

So, my question is whether it would be possible for lean core to restructure its imports in such a way that it is possible to use register_try?_tactic, try?, grind +suggestions and apply? without also importing a lot of redundant meta code.

• register_try?_tactic currently is in essence a macro that relies on being able to produce some code that mentions a couple of meta things. I'm not quite sure why it was chosen to implement it that way, as opposed to keeping a set of Syntax around but that is the reason it requires some imports. We can cut the amount of transitive imports required by this down by ~50% pretty easily by special casing the situation where the Try.Info argument is not used which leaves us with Lean.Meta.Basic and Lean.Parser.Extension as the only required imports.
  • For grind +suggestions I would suggest instead of erroring out when no engine is registered we just use the default engine instead of requiring an import that registers it.
  • I'm not quite sure about your apply? point, it just works without any imports ? e.g. https://live.lean-lang.org/#codez=KYDwhgtgDgNsAEAKAdvC8Bc8ByYAuAlJvKgNRrwC8F5qG1ARgJ7xhSxMD8QA

CC @Kim Morrison who is the author of the first two features.

The point with apply? is that the implementation of mathlib's observe tactic imports the implementation of apply?. So observe should either be upstreamed, so that it can be a builtin tactic, or not imported in Mathlib.Tactic.Common.

One thing about the module system that I haven't fully understood yet is why usually meta imports need to be public. For example, it would be convenient to be able to only privately meta import Lean.Meta.Tactic.LibrarySearch, so that this can be used to implement observe, but doesn't slow down later files.

Another place where it would be nice to have smaller imports is in #40755, where there is a slowdown of 0.29%, mostly due to importing Lean.Server.FileWorker.RequestHandling, to access Lean.Server.FileWorker.findGoalsAt?, which brings in a bunch of transitive imports.

Generally, these imports need to be public because we might need their IR in downstream modules (we still need some parts even for precompiled code). However, it is true that we do not need their .oleans at least; all this is open to future optimizations
